error handlers for 404/500 returning JSON instead of HTML **Results**: Clean API contract that frontend can reliably consume; consistent error handling structure **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:42:00Z] **Additional Details**: ```python @app.route('/api/hello', methods=['GET']) def api_hello(): return jsonify({'message': f'Hello, {name}!', 'status': 'success'}) @app.errorhandler(404) def not_found(error): return jsonify({'error': 'Not found', 'status': 'error'}), 404 ``` ### Bootstrap CDN Integration Pattern **Pattern**: Use CDN-hosted Bootstrap with integrity hashes for fast, secure frontend framework delivery **Context**: Rapid application development without complex build tools or package management for frontend assets **Implementation**: Bootstrap 5.3.3 CSS and JS bundle loaded via jsdelivr CDN with SRI integrity attributes; custom CSS loaded after Bootstrap for override capability **Results**: Fast page loads; no frontend build pipeline needed; automatic caching via CDN; secure asset delivery **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:43:00Z] **Additional Details**: Enables rapid prototyping while maintaining production-ready security practices through integrity verification. ### Frontend-Backend API Integration Pattern **Pattern**: Use async/await with Fetch API for clean, modern JavaScript API calls with proper error handling **Context**: Interactive web applications requiring dynamic data loading and form submissions without page reloads **Implementation**: Created async functions for API calls with try/catch error handling; JSON content-type headers; dynamic DOM updates with response data; smooth scroll to results **Results**: Clean, readable async code; proper error handling with user feedback; smooth UX without page reloads **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:43:30Z] **Additional Details**: ```javascript async function testApiEndpoint() { try { const response = await fetch('/api/hello?name=User'); const data = await response.json(); // Update DOM with response } catch (error) { console.error('API Error:', error); // Show error to user } } ``` ### Environment Configuration Pattern **Pattern**: Use python-dotenv for environment-specific configuration with sample file for documentation **Context**: Applications requiring different configurations for development/production, especially secret management **Implementation**: Created .env.sample as documentation; python-dotenv loads .env file; os.getenv() with fallback defaults for development convenience **Results**: Secure secret management; clear configuration documentation; easy environment switching; development-friendly defaults **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:44:30Z] **Additional Details**: SECRET_KEY defaults to dev value but warns to change in production via naming convention. ## Project Development Practices ### Atomic File Creation Practice **Practice**: Create complete, functional files in single operations rather than incremental edits **Context**: Bootstrapping new projects where file structure and content are well-defined upfront **Implementation**: Each file (app.py, index.html, app.js, style.css) created in complete form with full functionality in one Write operation **Results**: Cleaner version control history; faster project setup; immediate functionality without iterative debugging **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:44:00Z] **Additional Details**: Particularly effective for standard patterns like Flask apps where structure is well-established; reduces back-and-forth edits and testing cycles. ### Progressive Enhancement Structure **Practice**: Build HTML structure first, then add JavaScript interactivity, then polish with CSS **Context**: Web application development requiring reliable fallback behavior and clear separation of concerns **Implementation**: Created semantic HTML with Bootstrap classes for basic styling; added JavaScript for interactivity; applied custom CSS for visual polish and animations **Results**: Application works without JavaScript (graceful degradation); clear layer separation enables easier maintenance; progressive enhancement ensures broader compatibility **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:44:00Z] **Additional Details**: HTML structure remains usable even if JavaScript fails; Bootstrap provides baseline responsive behavior. ### Flask Project Structure Convention **Practice**: Follow standard Flask directory conventions (static/, templates/, app.py at root) **Context**: Flask applications benefiting from community-standard structure for maintainability and onboarding **Implementation**: Created static/js/, static/css/, and templates/ directories; placed Flask app at root level; used url_for() for asset references **Results**: Standard structure familiar to Flask developers; url_for() provides correct paths in all deployment contexts; clear asset organization **Added**: [2025-10-22T14:41:00Z] **Additional Details**: Enables deployment flexibility (app can run from any path) and integrates well with Flask ecosystem tools. ### UI Asset Migration Practice **Practice**: Replace visual assets systematically by updating references, styling, and cleaning up obsolete files **Context**: UI refinement requiring asset format changes or branding updates without breaking functionality **Implementation**: Identified all asset references in templates; updated HTML to new asset path; adjusted CSS for format-specific styling changes; verified visual consistency; removed obsolete assets **Results**: Clean asset migration without broken references; improved visual presentation; no orphaned files **Added**: [2025-10-22T15:13:00Z] **Additional Details**: Three-step process ensures consistency: (1) update template references, (2) adjust styling for new format requirements, (3) clean up old assets.
